| [NOTE-032](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-032.md) v2 | Work capacity of channels with memory | The paper models agent and environment as coupled finite hidden-Markov channels. It defines the environment's work capacity C_work = max over agent models of ⟨H(A_t\|M_t) − H(S_t\|M_t)⟩_t (in k_BT ln 2 per round) and proves two things. First, for unifilar environments whose percepts ignore actions, the efficient agents are exactly the randomize-and-forget ∩ maximally-predictive ones, and C_work = log\|A\| − h(S). Second, one binary memoryless environment exists where predictive, max-entropy-action and efficient agents form three nonempty, pairwise-disjoint sets: every predictive agent extracts ≤ 0, uniform-random agents extract 1 − h(3/4) ≈ 0.189 bits, and the optimum is ½·log₂(3/4 + 1/√2) ≈ 0.272 bits, reached by a memoryless agent that plays action 0 with probability 1/√2. | Read |
| [NOTE-091](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-091.md) | Pernu — Mental causation via neuroprosthetics? | Neuroprosthetics does not support nonreductive physicalism. | [NOTE-114](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-114.md) v2 | SEP — Biological individuals | A survey that maps biological individuals by crossing two axes: organism / some parts of organisms / some groups of organisms, against living agent (physiological) / Darwinian (evolutionary) individual. | [NOTE-148](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-148.md) v2 | Baedke — The Organism (Cambridge Element) | Baedke treats "organism" as a nexus concept with an organizational dimension and a relational dimension, joined by the various kinds of biological individuality. He argues that the standard "persister" (self-maintenance, closure) criterion cannot single organisms out, because colonies, holobionts and ecosystems meet it too, and that organisms are also "overcomers", able to destabilize and reorganize their own closure. Organisms are then individuated relationally by tracing diachronic causal paths in the unrolled O/E model of Baedke et al. 2021 ([LIT-110](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-110.md)). The overcomer claim rests on three illustrative cases, anglerfish, sea slug and jumping ant, and is asserted, not shown, to hold of organisms only (p. 40). | Read |
